Will smartwatches be the next big gaming platform?

No. But, I also see no point in smart watches. They don't seem to do or be capable of doing anything that a smart phone can't do in a much easier to use package. I understand conspicuous consumerism and status symbols, but smart watches seem ridiculous.

I got a pebble for Christmas, and its fairly awesome. I can control music without getting my phone out or if its across the room plugged into my stereo, check/dismiss notifications from it, and check the calender and weather while I'm doing something else easier than I can with my phone. Its one of those thing that you really don't realize how useful it is until you use it for a while, though I see little need for anything more high-tech than the one I have.

I am sorta curious to how creative devs could get with this though. I could see it being used for asymmetrical multiplayer games, I've loved the idea asymmetry like this since the Dreamcast (for example, people playing Texas Hold-em' or any card game on a tablet with their hands on their watch.)

I don't like pulling my phone out every time I want to see a message or change my music, so I have a smart watch. They're not there to do complicated tasks (even though some might try to make them) - they're there to do simple things that you don't want to pull your phone out to do. Right now they're expensive, making their price hard to justify, but will be a lot more understandable when they're cheaper.
